# §O — Measurements, diagnostics and operational readout
**Authority and status.** This section is the operational measurement contract for CHD-3.4. It specifies VOL-D `VOLD-043..048` and `VOLD-080..084`, R31-012, and the measurement part of INDEX §5. A specification label records contract presence only; `implemented` is reserved for inspectable runtime code. Values labelled `measured` require a captured run. `proposed` is an operator budget, not a product guarantee; `unverified` means that no live adapter evidence is shipped.

## O.1 Evidence classes and status labels
| Class | Answers | Required evidence | Cannot prove | |---|---|---|---| | Sample evidence | What did this fixture/run observe? | Raw samples, request/response bodies, expected/observed records, config/fixture digest, run id | Specification conformance, production readiness or owner acceptance | | Specification checks | Does the authored contract/schema/matrix agree internally? | Validator output, schema/fixture checks, named source revision | Live runtime behavior or measured performance | | Measured runs | What did a finite repeatable workload consume? | Captured run, raw samples, window definition, restart snapshots, compact/reconstruct comparison | Authorization, semantic correctness, recovery or owner acceptance | | Owner acceptance | Has the configured owner accepted the objective? | Criterion-by-criterion evidence and configured approval record | A green build, counter, status label or fixture pass alone |
Every report carries independent status fields: `specified`, `internally_checked`, `source_cross_checked`, `implemented`, `measured`, and `owner_accepted`. The words `proposed` and `unverified` qualify the evidence class; they never upgrade another status. A performance result never closes a correctness, authorization, recovery or owner-acceptance cell. A fixture pass demonstrates the test adapter only.

## O.2 Retention-safe metric contract
The collector MUST NOT derive lifetime totals from rows that are about to be tombstoned. Before compaction, it writes an immutable `MetricCheckpoint` record (`schemas/metric-checkpoint.schema.json`) and advances a source watermark. A checkpoint contains the metric, bounded labels, label schema version, source kind, scope, dedupe epoch, bucket values and the last committed namespace/sequence/event watermark. The checkpoint is the retention-independent lifetime source; the original rows may then be compacted or tombstoned without making `since_start` totals fall.
A metric event uses a deterministic idempotency key: `metric_name + canonical_label_bytes + source_record_id + source_revision + event_kind`. The collector stores the key or its covered hash in the checkpoint's dedupe epoch. Replayed pages, a retry after collector restart, and a checkpoint rebuild therefore contribute zero additional count. A checkpoint is committed before any source row that it covers is tombstoned; if the checkpoint write or read-back fails, compaction stops and the source rows remain. Checkpoints are append-only and addressed by `checkpoint_id`; an operator reset creates a new `run_id`/epoch and audit record, never mutating historical checkpoints.
The event/aggregate choice is explicit. Event-backed metrics use the durable `MetricEvent` source and checkpoint-plus-events reconstruction. State-backed gauges and capacity use canonical state reconstruction and never infer state from a counter. The collector startup sequence is: acquire the writer lease; load the newest checkpoint; scan committed events after its watermark with a stable cursor; reconcile the canonical attempt/run state; write a restart readback; then publish status. A missing or conflicting checkpoint yields `unverified`/`null` with a reason, not zero.

### O.2.1 Metric register
Every row names the source labels, canonical state, dedupe key, retention, schema migration, restart/reconstruction rule and query output. Labels are closed enums or bounded identifiers; request text, URLs, arbitrary exceptions and user text are never labels. `send_id`, `attempt_id`, and `run_id` remain correlation fields, not interchangeable label sources.
| Metric | Source labels | Canonical attempt/run state | Dedupe | Retention and migration | Restart/reconstruction | Query output | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | `chd_requests_total` | `operation`, `result` | committed request claim/audit decision | request id + revision + result | checkpoint before 90d request tombstone; v1→v2 maps result enum, explicit gap on unknown | checkpoint + MetricEvent after watermark | `/v1/status?view=metrics` with `scope=since_start`, `checkpoint_id`, `as_of` | | `chd_send_state_total` | `from_state`, `to_state` | SendManifest transition revision | send id + manifest revision + transition | checkpoint before terminal-manifest tombstone; preserve transition enum; unknown migration is a gap | checkpoint + transition events | `/chd/send?view=metrics&state=` and status | | `chd_worker_runs_total` | `state`, bounded `role` | WorkerRun state/revision; terminal state is not inferred from report | run id + state revision | checkpoint before run retention; v1 state aliases map to canonical state, never drop `unknown` | checkpoint + run events; reconcile open runs first | `/v1/runs?view=metrics&state=` | | `chd_worker_run_seconds` | bounded `role`, terminal `state` | WorkerRun with `started_at` and `ended_at` | run id + terminal revision | raw sample/checkpoint retained 90d; non-finite/unknown remains a gap | reconstruct only from canonical timestamps; no duration from logs | run record plus status histogram with `sample_status` | | `chd_waits_total` | `gate`, `state` (`opened`,`resolved`,`cancelled`,`open`) | WaitRecord state; `open` is a current state, not a completed event | wait id + state revision | checkpoint before wait tombstone; preserve open/held rows and migration aliases | checkpoint + wait events; current open set from WaitRecord | `/chd/wait?view=metrics&state=` | | `chd_report_results_total` | fixed `result`, bounded `agent` | ReportEnvelope tied to send/attempt/run | report id + verdict revision; exact replay returns same result | checkpoint before envelope retention; changed second report remains separate refusal event | checkpoint + report events | `/chd/report?view=metrics&result=` | | `chd_capacity_inflight` | `gateway`, `dimension` (`attempt`,`run`,`session`) | canonical Attempt/Run state: `admitted`, `dispatched`, `running`, `paused:uncertain`, `paused:unreachable` charge; only `proven-stopped` releases | reservation id + attempt id + run revision | open/uncertain reservations retained until proven stop; closed snapshots 30d; state aliases migrate to canonical set | reconstruct from active manifests, attempts and runs; uncertain stays visible | `/v1/capacity` returns `charged`, `uncertain`, `held`, `as_of`, source refs | | `chd_archive_results_total` | `operation`, fixed `result`, bounded `agent` | ExportManifest/checkpoint publication state | export id + checkpoint revision | checkpoint/gap manifest retained 90d; unsupported schema is explicit gap | checkpoint + archive events | `/chd/archive/status?view=metrics` | | `chd_bridge_deliveries_total` | `direction`, fixed `result` | durable delivery/ACK record | delivery id + outcome revision | checkpoint before dead-letter retention; old result aliases map or gap | checkpoint + delivery events; ACK-before-commit is error | `/chd/bridge/status?view=metrics` | | `chd_fixture_steps_total` | `scenario` (`WF-01`..`WF-10`), `result` | evidence report step and observed record | run id + step id + observation digest | evidence report is authoritative and retained; schema migration preserves expected/observed | checkpoint index + report readback; no fabricated zero | `evidence/runs/<run>/report.json` | | `chd_cycle_cost_tokens` | `cycle_phase` (`startup`,`unchanged`,`recovery`), bounded `role` | measurement run/cycle boundary, not a send state | measurement run id + cycle ordinal + sample digest | raw samples/checkpoint retained 90d; incompatible unit is `unverified` | reconstruct from retained samples/checkpoint only | soak report with `evidence_class=measured` |
The same label source is used in status, audit and evidence queries: `send_id` identifies a logical send, `attempt_id` identifies one dispatch episode, and `run_id` identifies one external execution. A report or wait cannot silently substitute one for another. `chd_capacity_inflight` is charged from the canonical Attempt/Run state table, not from `SendManifest` closure, lease expiry, report arrival, or a collector-local counter. Unknown/uncertain runs retain their reservation and appear as `uncertain`/`held`; they are never hidden as zero.

## O.3 Events, open-state labels and logs
Every durable `MetricEvent` contains `event_id`, `event_type` from a closed enum, `occurred_at`, `schema_version`, `run_id` when applicable, correlation refs (`send_id`, `attempt_id`, `run_id`), bounded labels, `source_record_id`, source revision, dedupe key/digest, value, and `record_refs`. Logs are diagnostic projections, not authority. The authoritative sequence is the durable event or canonical record plus its read-back response.
Open states are printed rather than collapsed: `queued`, `admitted`, `dispatched`, `running`, `await_report`, `waiting_human`, `paused:unreachable`, `paused:uncertain`, and `open` are active labels; `terminal` is not. Every open label must resolve to the canonical state machine for its record family. The readout includes `state_source` (`attempt` or `run` for capacity, `wait` for wait, `send` for send) and `as_of` watermark. A NULL value includes a reason such as `store_unavailable`, `checkpoint_missing`, `schema_gap`, or `no_sample`; it is not printed as zero.

## O.4 Migration, compaction and reconstruction acceptance
Schema migration is additive and versioned. A collector supports the current checkpoint schema and one previous version; it rewrites a migrated checkpoint under an append-only new `checkpoint_id`, records `from_schema_version`, transform and loss (`none` or `explicit_gap`), and never silently discards an unknown label/state. Compaction ordering is: stop metric publication; acquire writer lease; flush and read back MetricEvent batches; write and read back checkpoint; verify watermark and label digest; only then tombstone covered counted rows; restart collector; reconstruct from checkpoint plus post-watermark events and canonical open state; compare with the pre-compaction report. Any mismatch is `unverified` and blocks deletion.
The required evidence sequence is **measure → compact/tombstone → restart collector → reconstruct → compare**. `since_start` totals must be monotone (equal or greater), rolling windows must expire by event timestamp rather than compaction, duplicate replay must be stable, and uncertain capacity must remain visible and charged. The acceptance fixture must include one duplicate event, one old rolling-window event, one tombstoned terminal record, one open wait, and one uncertain run.

## O.5 Bounded comparison and provisional workload
For a repeatable unchanged-workload comparison, use two finite windows of five identical cycles (`window_cycles=5`) and a stated tolerance of 10%. Compare the later median with the earlier median; pass if the later median is no more than `earlier × 1.10`. Report startup separately. A steady-state band is a band, not a strictly decreasing sequence. The eight-cycle figure is only a **provisional** burn budget for four fires per day over two days, not a token law and not a universal ceiling. No acceptance criterion requires tokens to decrease from cycle to cycle.
A cycle starts at the named director fire and ends when all its sends are terminal or waiting. Record config digest, fixture revision, seed, cadence, raw samples, counter snapshots before/after, compact/tombstone result and restart readback. A single sample never carries a performance verdict.

## O.6 Operational readout and traceability
The operator readout shows readiness, config/fixture digest, writer lease, capacity by gateway and canonical attempt/run state, open sends and waits, held uncertain capacity, archive gaps, bridge dead letters, last successful durable readback, checkpoint/watermark and links to retained evidence. It labels each claim `sample`, `specified`, `internally_checked`, `measured`, `proposed`, `unverified`, or `owner_accepted`.
A green build or passing count is not acceptance. Page on an accepted request without fsync/readback, denial without audit, capacity above cap, unknown run released without stop proof, report closed on wrong correlation, archive restore without lineage, or ACK before local durable write. Preserve evidence and stop the affected scope; never repair a counter by editing it.
`matrices/test-matrix.csv` maps critical failure gates to named probes; `harness/run_scenario.py` emits expected versus observed effects and retains reports and records. R32-024 requires the WF-07 evidence to retain the sequence `measure → compact/tombstone → restart → reconstruct → compare`, with separate sample, specification-check, measured-run and owner-acceptance fields.
